questions.q: Two observables $A$ and $B$ commute. This implies that
options: they possess a common complete set of eigenstates
they can never be measured exactly
questions.explain: If $[A,B]=0$ they can be diagonalised simultaneously, so a state can be a joint eigenstate with sharp values of both. Conservation requires $[H,A]=0$, which is a different condition.

questions.q: The generalised uncertainty relation $\Delta A\,\Delta B\ge\tfrac12|\langle[A,B]\rangle|$ is state dependent because
options: the commutator's expectation value $\langle[A,B]\rangle$ is evaluated in the state $|\psi\rangle$
$\Delta A$ depends on the measurement apparatus
it is only valid for Gaussian states
questions.explain: It follows from the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for $|\psi\rangle$. For $[x,p]=i\hbar$ the right side is state independent, $\hbar/2$, but e.g. for $[L_x,L_y]=i\hbar L_z$ it equals $\tfrac\hbar2|\langle L_z\rangle|$.

questions.q: Physical observables are represented by Hermitian operators because
options: Hermitian operators have real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors
questions.explain: $A=A^\dagger$ gives $\langle\psi|A|\psi\rangle\in\mathbb R$, real eigenvalues (the measurement results), and orthogonality of eigenvectors with different eigenvalues, which is needed for the Born rule. Without Hermiticity the measured values could be complex and the probabilities $|\langle a_i|\psi\rangle|^2$ would not sum to one.

questions.q: Inside a classically forbidden barrier the wave function decays exponentially because
options: the particle loses energy to the barrier
the probability current is negative inside
for $E<V_0$ the wave number is imaginary, $k=i\kappa$ with $\kappa=\sqrt{2m(V_0-E)}/\hbar$
questions.explain: The Schrödinger equation $\psi''=\kappa^2\psi$ has real exponential solutions $e^{\pm\kappa x}$. For a wide barrier the transmission is $T\approx e^{-2\kappa a}$, with $a$ the width.

questions.q: The energies of the infinite square well scale as $E_n\propto n^2$ because
options: the energy levels are equally spaced
questions.explain: $\psi(0)=\psi(L)=0$ gives standing waves $\sin(n\pi x/L)$, so $E_n=\frac{\hbar^2\pi^2n^2}{2mL^2}$. The harmonic oscillator, by contrast, has equal spacing.

questions.q: The zero-point energy $\hbar\omega/2$ of the harmonic oscillator arises because
options: the ground state has a node
the potential has a minimum at $x=0$
localising the particle costs momentum spread ($[x,p]=i\hbar$), so $\langle H\rangle$ cannot vanish
questions.explain: With $\Delta x\Delta p\ge\hbar/2$ the energy $\langle H\rangle\ge\frac{\hbar^2}{8m\Delta x^2}+\tfrac12m\omega^2\Delta x^2$ has the minimum $\hbar\omega/2$ at $\Delta x^2=\hbar/2m\omega$. Without the uncertainty relation the particle could sit at $x=0$ with $p=0$ and $E=0$, so $E_0>0$ is a purely quantum effect.

questions.q: The spectrum of $N=a^\dagger a$ is bounded below by 0 because
questions.explain: The norm of $a|\psi\rangle$ is non-negative, so $n\ge0$. Since $a$ lowers $n$ by one, the chain must end at a state with $a|0\rangle=0$, which makes $n$ a non-negative integer.

questions.q: The first-order energy shift in non-degenerate perturbation theory is
questions.explain: To first order in $H'$ the energy shift is the expectation value of $H'$ in the unperturbed state. The sum with energy denominators is the second-order shift $E_n^{(2)}$.

questions.q: For a degenerate level one must diagonalise $H'$ within the degenerate subspace because
options: the energy denominators $E_n-E_m$ vanish, so the correct zeroth-order states are eigenstates of $H'$ in the subspace
the perturbation removes the Pauli principle
questions.explain: Ordinary second-order formulas diverge for $E_m=E_n$. Choosing the basis in which $H'$ is diagonal in the subspace makes off-diagonal terms vanish and the first-order shifts are the eigenvalues of $H'$.

questions.q: The eigenvalue of $\mathbf L^2$ is $\hbar^2l(l+1)$ rather than $\hbar^2l^2$ because
questions.explain: $\mathbf L^2=L_x^2+L_y^2+L_z^2$ and for $m=l$ the transverse part has the eigenvalue $\hbar^2l$ because $[L_x,L_y]\ne0$ forbids all three components from being sharp: $l(l+1)=l^2+l$. Check with $l=1$: $\mathbf L^2=2\hbar^2$ while $L_z^2\le\hbar^2$, so the angular momentum vector never points exactly along $z$.

questions.q: A spin-up-$z$ beam passes through an $x$-filter and then a $z$-analyser. Half of it ends up spin-down because
options: the $x$-filter flips half the spins magnetically
questions.explain: $|{+x}\rangle=(|{\uparrow}\rangle+|{\downarrow}\rangle)/\sqrt2$, so after the $x$-filter the $z$-probabilities are $1/2$ each. This is the sequential Stern–Gerlach experiment.

questions.q: Two identical spin-1/2 fermions in the same spatial orbital must be in the
questions.explain: The total wave function must be antisymmetric under exchange. A symmetric spatial part therefore needs an antisymmetric spin part, which is the singlet. This is the Pauli principle.

questions.q: An observable $A$ without explicit time dependence is conserved if and only if
questions.explain: From $\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\langle A\rangle=\frac{i}{\hbar}\langle[H,A]\rangle$ (Ehrenfest) the expectation value is constant for all states exactly when $[H,A]=0$. Example: for a free particle $[H,p]=0$ so $p$ is conserved, but $[H,x]\ne0$ so $\langle x\rangle$ moves.

questions.q: The width $a$ of a wide barrier is increased by 50 %. The transmission $T\approx e^{-2\kappa a}$ becomes about
questions.explain: The exponent is linear in $a$, so $e^{-2\kappa(1.5a)}=(e^{-2\kappa a})^{1.5}=T^{3/2}$. The transmission drops much faster than linearly.

questions.q: The mass of the tunnelling particle is quadrupled (same $E$, $V_0$, $a$). The transmission $T\approx e^{-2\kappa a}$ becomes
questions.explain: $\kappa=\sqrt{2m(V_0-E)}/\hbar\propto\sqrt m$, so $\kappa\to2\kappa$ and the exponent doubles, $T\to T^2$. That is why proton tunnelling is far less likely than electron tunnelling.

questions.q: The STM tip is retracted by $0.1$ nm (work function $\phi=4.5$ eV, $I\propto e^{-2\kappa d}$). The current falls by a factor of about
questions.explain: $\kappa=\sqrt{2m\phi}/\hbar=1.09\times10^{10}$ m$^{-1}$, so $e^{-2\kappa\cdot0.1\,\mathrm{nm}}=e^{-2.18}=0.113$, a factor 9. This extreme sensitivity gives the STM atomic resolution.

questions.q: The mass of a harmonic oscillator is quadrupled while the spring constant is kept. The level spacing $\hbar\omega$ becomes
questions.explain: $\omega=\sqrt{k/m}$, so $m\to4m$ gives $\omega\to\omega/2$. The spacing $\hbar\omega=\hbar\sqrt{k/m}$ scales as $m^{-1/2}$, so quadrupling $m$ halves it.

questions.q: A constant force is added: $H=H_0-Fx$. The exact spectrum is
questions.explain: Completing the square, $\tfrac12m\omega^2(x-x_0)^2-F^2/2m\omega^2$ with $x_0=F/m\omega^2$. The first-order shift $-F\langle x\rangle$ vanishes by parity, and the second-order shift gives the exact result.

questions.q: The width $L$ of an infinite square well is doubled. The ground-state energy changes by a factor
questions.explain: $E_1=\pi^2\hbar^2/2mL^2\propto L^{-2}$. Doubling $L$ therefore gives $E_1\to E_1/2^2=E_1/4$.

questions.q: A spin-1/2 particle's magnetic field is doubled. The Larmor frequency $\omega_L=\gamma B$ and the Zeeman splitting
options: $\omega_L$ doubles and the splitting is unchanged
questions.explain: The Zeeman Hamiltonian $H=-\gamma BS_z$ has levels $\mp\hbar\gamma B/2$, giving a splitting $\hbar\omega_L$ that is linear in $B$. The spin precesses at $\omega_L$.

questions.q: The electron mass in hydrogen is hypothetically doubled. The binding energy and the Bohr radius change as
questions.explain: $E_n=-\frac{m e^4}{2(4\pi\epsilon_0)^2\hbar^2n^2}\propto m$ and $a_0=\frac{4\pi\epsilon_0\hbar^2}{me^2}\propto1/m$ (with the reduced mass in practice). Hence doubling $m$ doubles $|E_n|$ and halves $a_0$.

questions.q: A perturbation $\lambda H'$ is doubled ($\lambda\to2\lambda$). The first- and second-order energy shifts change by factors
questions.explain: $E^{(1)}\propto\lambda$ and $E^{(2)}\propto\lambda^2$, since $E_n=E_n^{(0)}+\lambda E^{(1)}+\lambda^2E^{(2)}+\dots$. So the factors are $2^1=2$ and $2^2=4$.

questions.q: Two non-interacting identical spinless particles occupy an infinite well. The ground-state energy in units of $E_1$ is, for bosons and fermions respectively,
questions.explain: Bosons both occupy $n=1$: $2E_1$. Fermions need different orbitals, $n=1$ and $2$ with $E_n=n^2E_1$, so $E_1+4E_1=5E_1$.

questions.q: $S_z$ is measured and gives $+\hbar/2$. If it is measured again immediately, the outcome is
questions.explain: The measurement projects the state onto the eigenstate $|{\uparrow}\rangle$. A second, identical measurement has probability $|\langle\uparrow|\uparrow\rangle|^2=1$.

questions.q: The Hamiltonian commutes with the parity operator and the initial state is even. At later times the state is
options: a superposition of even and odd
questions.explain: $[H,\Pi]=0$ gives $\Pi U(t)=U(t)\Pi$, so $\Pi|\psi(t)\rangle=U(t)\Pi|\psi(0)\rangle=+|\psi(t)\rangle$. Parity is a conserved quantity.

questions.q: The mass of a free Gaussian wave packet is increased. Its spreading $\Delta x(t)^2=\Delta x_0^2+(\hbar t/2m\Delta x_0)^2$ becomes
questions.explain: The spreading term is inversely proportional to $m$: heavy particles have a smaller velocity spread $\Delta v=\hbar/2m\Delta x_0$. At fixed $t$ the extra width $\hbar t/(2m\Delta x_0)$ shrinks as $1/m$, so the packet spreads more slowly.

questions.q: An electron has kinetic energy $100$ eV. Its de Broglie wavelength $\lambda=h/\sqrt{2mE}$ is about
questions.explain: $\lambda=1.226\,\mathrm{nm}/\sqrt{E/\mathrm{eV}}=0.123$ nm, which is of the order of atomic spacings. This is why low-energy electrons diffract from crystals.

questions.q: The H$\alpha$ line ($n=3\to2$) of hydrogen has the wavelength of about
questions.explain: $1/\lambda=R_\infty(1/4-1/9)$ with $R_\infty=1.0974\times10^7$ m$^{-1}$ gives $\lambda=656$ nm. The Lyman $\alpha$ (122 nm) is $n=2\to1$ and the Paschen $\alpha$ (1875 nm) is $n=4\to3$.

questions.q: An electron with $E=1$ eV hits a barrier $V_0=2$ eV of width $0.5$ nm. The estimate $T\approx e^{-2\kappa a}$ gives about
questions.explain: $\kappa=\sqrt{2m(V_0-E)}/\hbar=5.12\times10^9$ m$^{-1}$ and $2\kappa a=5.12$, so $T\approx e^{-5.12}=5.9\times10^{-3}$. Because $T$ depends exponentially on $a$, an extra 0.1 nm of width lowers $T$ by $e^{-1.0}$, which is the principle of the STM.

questions.q: The CO molecule has $k=1860$ N m$^{-1}$ and reduced mass $\mu=1.14\times10^{-26}$ kg. The vibrational spacing $\hbar\omega$ is about
questions.explain: $\omega=\sqrt{k/\mu}=4.04\times10^{14}$ s$^{-1}$ and $\hbar\omega=0.266$ eV, which is in the infrared ($4.6$ $\mu$m). Since $\hbar\omega\gg k_BT=0.026$ eV at 300 K, CO sits in its vibrational ground state at room temperature.

questions.q: An electron is confined to $\Delta x=0.1$ nm. With $\Delta p=\hbar/2\Delta x$, the kinetic energy estimate $\Delta p^2/2m$ is about
questions.explain: $E=\hbar^2/(8m\Delta x^2)=1.5\times10^{-19}$ J $=0.95$ eV, comparable to the binding energies in atoms. This is the confinement (zero-point) energy scale, which is why atomic binding energies of a few eV are natural.

questions.q: An electron in an infinite well of width $L=1$ nm has a ground-state energy $\pi^2\hbar^2/2mL^2$ of about
questions.explain: $E_1=\pi^2\hbar^2/(2mL^2)=0.376$ eV. The levels scale as $E_n=n^2E_1$.

questions.q: The electron-spin resonance frequency $\nu=2\mu_BB/h$ at $B=1$ T is about
questions.explain: $\nu=g\mu_BB/h=2\cdot9.274\times10^{-24}/6.626\times10^{-34}=2.80\times10^{10}$ Hz, in the microwave regime (X band: 9 GHz at 0.33 T). For comparison $\nu/B=28$ GHz/T, the electron analogue of the NMR Larmor frequency.

questions.q: The fine-structure splitting of the $2P$ level in hydrogen, $\alpha^2\cdot13.6\,\mathrm{eV}/16$, is about
questions.explain: With $\alpha=1/137.036$, $\alpha^2=5.33\times10^{-5}$ and $\alpha^2\cdot13.606/16=4.5\times10^{-5}$ eV, the splitting between $2P_{3/2}$ and $2P_{1/2}$ (10.9 GHz). It is smaller than the Bohr energy $E_2=3.4$ eV by $\sim\alpha^2/4\sim10^{-5}$, so it is a small perturbation.

questions.q: The reduced Compton wavelength of the electron, $\hbar/m_ec$, is about
questions.explain: $\hbar/(m_ec)=1.0546\times10^{-34}/(9.109\times10^{-31}\cdot2.998\times10^8)=3.86\times10^{-13}$ m. It is $\alpha a_0$, smaller than the Bohr radius ($5.3\times10^{-11}$ m) by a factor 137.

questions.q: A thermal neutron ($T=300$ K, $E=\tfrac32k_BT$) has a de Broglie wavelength of about
questions.explain: $p=\sqrt{3m_nk_BT}=4.6\times10^{-24}$ kg m s$^{-1}$ and $\lambda=h/p=1.45\times10^{-10}$ m. This is the lattice spacing, which makes neutron diffraction possible.

questions.q: Which operator is Hermitian?
questions.explain: The momentum $\hat p=-i\hbar\,\mathrm d/\mathrm dx$ is Hermitian, so $i\,\mathrm d/\mathrm dx=-\hat p/\hbar$ is as well. $\mathrm d/\mathrm dx$ is anti-Hermitian, and $\hat x\hat p$ is not Hermitian since $[\hat x,\hat p]\ne0$.

questions.q: The commutator $[\hat x,\hat p^2]$ equals
questions.explain: $[x,p^2]=[x,p]p+p[x,p]=2i\hbar p$ by the Leibniz rule.

questions.q: The commutator $[L_z,L_x]$ equals
questions.explain: The algebra is cyclic, $[L_i,L_j]=i\hbar\epsilon_{ijk}L_k$, and $(z,x,y)$ is a cyclic permutation of $(x,y,z)$, so the sign is $+$.

questions.q: The spin-1/2 state $(|{\uparrow}\rangle+|{\downarrow}\rangle)/\sqrt2$ is an eigenstate of $S_x$ with the eigenvalue
questions.explain: $S_x=\frac\hbar2\sigma_x$ and $\sigma_x(1,1)^T=(1,1)^T$, so the eigenvalue is $+\hbar/2$. In contrast, $\langle S_z\rangle=0$ in this state.

questions.q: A particle in an infinite well is in the state $(\psi_1+\psi_2)/\sqrt2$. The expectation value of the energy is
questions.explain: $\langle H\rangle=\tfrac12(E_1+E_2)$ with $E_2=4E_1$. It is not the geometric mean, and the energy is never found to be $5E_1/2$ in a measurement.

questions.q: The degeneracy of the hydrogen level $n=3$ (ignoring spin) is
questions.explain: $\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^2=9$. Including spin it would be $2n^2=18$.

questions.q: In the oscillator ground state, $\langle x^2\rangle$ equals
questions.explain: With $x=\sqrt{\hbar/2m\omega}\,(a+a^\dagger)$, $\langle0|x^2|0\rangle=\frac{\hbar}{2m\omega}\langle0|aa^\dagger|0\rangle=\frac{\hbar}{2m\omega}$. Check: $\langle V\rangle=\frac12m\omega^2\langle x^2\rangle=\hbar\omega/4=E_0/2$, as the virial theorem requires.

questions.q: Which transition in hydrogen is electric-dipole allowed?
questions.explain: The dipole selection rules are $\Delta l=\pm1$ and $\Delta m=0,\pm1$. Only $3d\to2p$ obeys $\Delta l=\pm1$ of the choices listed.

questions.q: The parity of the state $|n,l,m\rangle$ of hydrogen with $l=2$ is
questions.explain: Under $\mathbf r\to-\mathbf r$ the spherical harmonics transform as $Y_{lm}\to(-1)^lY_{lm}$, so $l=2$ is even. In general the parity of $|n,l,m\rangle$ is $(-1)^l$: s and d states are even, p and f states odd.

questions.q: In a stationary state, the expectation value of any observable $A$ without explicit time dependence is
questions.explain: $|\psi(t)\rangle=e^{-iEt/\hbar}|\psi_E\rangle$, so the global phase cancels in $\langle\psi|A|\psi\rangle$. Time dependence needs superpositions of different energies.

questions.q: The variational principle states that for any normalised trial state $|\phi\rangle$
questions.explain: Expanding $|\phi\rangle=\sum c_n|n\rangle$ gives $\sum|c_n|^2E_n\ge E_0\sum|c_n|^2=E_0$. The estimate is an upper bound on the ground-state energy.

questions.q: In degenerate perturbation theory with $H'=\begin{pmatrix}0&V\\V&0\end{pmatrix}$ in a two-fold degenerate level $E_0$, the first-order energies are
questions.explain: The eigenvalues of $H'$ in the subspace are $\pm|V|$ with eigenvectors $(1,\pm1)/\sqrt2$, so the degeneracy is lifted linearly in $V$. The correct zeroth-order states are therefore the symmetric and antisymmetric combinations, not the original basis states.
